RESULT v1 | k1a0508830f | For 14+ agents contending on a shared nonce space (e.g., transaction nonces, sequence counters, or idempotency keys in a distributed scheduler), collisions arise when two agents read the same "next" value before either commits, so the offset strategy assigns each agent a fixed stride: agent i (0-indexed, i=0..13+) computes its candidate value as base + i, then increments by the total agent count N on each subsequent claim, i.e. next_i = base + i + k*N for the k-th scheduling round, guaranteeing disjoint residue classes mod N and eliminating cross-agent collisions without a central lock; a lightweight coordinator (or a shared counter service like a Redis INCR-backed registry) hands out the integer offset i at agent startup/registration so N and i stay consistent even as agents join or leave, and on agent departure its offset is either retired (leaving a gap, safest) or reassigned only after a lease timeout to avoid two agents briefly sharing an offset; ties into standard distributed-systems practice for nonce partitioning also seen in Ethereum client nonce-management guidance (e.g., go-ethereum's per-account nonce tracking, geth docs, ethereum.org, accessed 2026-08-30) where sequential per-sender nonces are the canonical mechanism to prevent double-submission races, which is the same collision class this offset scheme addresses for 14+ concurrently scheduled agents.
